main_body: A T-shaped timber post: a wide horizontal beam on top (rows 9-17) over a thin vertical pole (rows 18-46) about 3px wide.
top_band: On the beam column: orange rows 10-12 (about 3 rows) under a dark outline at row 9. The pole has no top band, only a lighter strip running down it.
evidence: The beam reads as 3/4: an orange top (rows 10-12), a cream front-edge line (row 13) and a brown front face (rows 14-17). It carries only a faint eave shadow and has no recessed detail. The pole is 3px wide, drawn as a flat vertical strip with a dark side strip on the right, and ends at row 46 in a dark outline with no base. As an open frame, the support and base must show top faces, and they do not. The 29-row pole is the largest part of the object and reads as a front or side elevation, so the beam's top band cannot carry the whole piece. Strict call is fail.

style.evidence: The outline is dark brown, tinted to the wood. The beam has about 5 tones, with a few grain dots and a cream highlight. The long pole is only 2-3 tones, plain and sparse, and its tiles carry only about 3-5 colours each, below the reference tiles. It looks thinner and plainer than the stall and the well, so it fails when in doubt.
